_about: Comments placed on the page at build time. `quote` must appear verbatim (whitespace-insensitive) in the built page text; the build warns if it does not. New comments from reviewers go to the storage backend, never here.

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.quote: The Tri-agency instructions ask you to explain your role in each contribution and leave the grammatical person open.
comments.text: F-1, proposed replacement pending Eli's sign-off: "Yes. The Tri-agency instructions ask you to explain your role in each contribution and leave the grammatical person open. Concordia recommends the first person because it states your role most directly. If every sentence says 'we,' reviewers cannot tell what you did." Basis: the SSHRC and CIHR instructions, checked on 2026-09-21, ask for "your role in each contribution or experience" and contain no first-person wording.

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.text: F-9, proposed replacement pending Eli's sign-off: "The main change is rhetorical. A Narrative CV asks you to explain your contributions as well as list them, and to make your own role visible in each one." Active voice is a means; the instructions ask for a visible role.

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.quote: French or English. The FRQ application form itself must be completed in French.
comments.text: F-2, answered 2026-09-22. The old cell read "French required for most programs", which was wrong. FRQ presentation standards: "The pre-application and application forms must be filled out in French. The documents attached to the form can be written in either French or English." The CV-FRQ instructions (July 2026, the authoritative French text) set a limit for an English CV: "Le CV descriptif ne doit pas excéder 6 pages (ou 5 pages en version anglaise)." The cell now says so (P-32). One point still worth confirming with the FRQ: in competitions on the new FRQnet portal the CV is completed directly in the "CV-FRQ" section of the application rather than attached. The instructions keep the English page limit without distinguishing the two portals, which indicates English is accepted there too, but it is the one case the standards' wording (forms in French, attachments in either language) does not settle outright. Program rules can also add requirements.

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.quote: the Tri-agency is gradually implementing the Tri-agency CV (TCV) requirement over a few years.
comments.text: F-5: The 2021 date is unverified, and "has since expanded" is softer than the current picture. CIHR (2026-03-19) will not use the TCV for the Project Grant before Fall 2027 at the earliest; SSHRC requires it in Destination Horizon, Knowledge Synthesis and Impact Awards. Should this sentence name the competitions that currently use the TCV, with a date?

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.quote: Four qualities help reviewers find them in your CV:
comments.text: F-10: Is "consistently score higher" based on review outcome data or on workshop experience? If the former, the basis should be cited. If the latter, the sentence should say so.

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.quote: Funders that currently use narrative CV formats:
comments.text: F-17: Wellcome does not appear in our sourced scan of narrative CV formats; UKRI and NWO do. Can you point to Wellcome's format, or should it come off the list?

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.text: F-19: This example is invented. On an official Concordia page it reads as a real case, it names Indigenous organizations and the City, and a food-security protocol is paired with a housing strategy. Is there a real example, usable with consent, that could replace it?

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.quote: Not permitted: the CV must be self-contained.
comments.text: F-21, answered 2026-09-22. The rule is in the reviewer guidelines, not the applicant instructions: 'Guidelines for reviewing the tri-agency CV', section 5, 'Self-contained information' (CIHR, cihr-irsc.gc.ca/e/54339.html; NSERC publishes the same text). It reads: "The sole exception for which other sources may be permitted is for hyperlinks, but only if they are used to demonstrate audio/visual creative outputs, if applicable for specific funding opportunities." and "However, there is no guarantee that hyperlinks will be accessed." The cell now carries both conditions (P-31). Note for the NSERC conversation: NSERC's Research Portal presentation standards say "Do not include hyperlinks or bookmarks in your documents", which does not allow the exception its own reviewer guidelines grant.

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.quote: please contact the Pathways to Impact team at
comments.text: Q-4: Concordia's house style names a person with their title. Is there a named narrative CV advisor to put here?

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-21)
comments.text: Q-1: Capitalisation is mixed on the page: "Narrative CV" appears 12 times and "narrative CV" three times. The agencies, Concordia's FAQ and the builder page use lower case in running text. Which rule should the page follow?

comments.author: Claude (review, 2026-09-22)
comments.quote: NSERC requires 12-point Times New Roman for all text, including references and tables.
comments.text: F-22: NSERC told Prem on 2026-09-22 that the TCV allows no font exception for tables and references. NSERC's own published presentation standards say the opposite in a footnote: "Font and size rules do not apply to text within tables and figures. However, the font must be clearly legible." (Research Portal and NSERC Online presentation and attachment standards, read 2026-09-22.) We have published the stricter rule, because following it cannot make an application non-compliant either way. Worth getting NSERC's position in writing, and asking whether their published standards will be updated. Verified the same day: SSHRC requires "12-point, Arial font in black type" with the exception; NSERC requires 12-point Times New Roman; the CV-FRQ requires "Times New Roman (12 points)".
